{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the giving and taking frames would have asymmetric effects on allocations depending on dictator gender, specifically that female dictators would allocate more to recipients in the taking frame compared to the giving frame.",
  "design": "between-subject, with two treatments: Giving game versus Taking game, crossed with dictator gender (male vs. female)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "experimental frame (Giving game where the dictator decides how much of £10 to give to a recipient vs. Taking game where the dictator decides how much of £10 to take for themselves from the recipient) and dictator gender",
  "outcome_measure": "amount allocated to the recipient (amount given in the giving game, or £10 minus the amount taken in the taking game)",
  "population_and_setting": "students at the University of East Anglia participating in a computerized laboratory experiment",
  "sample_size_total": 280,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "recruited randomly through the online recruitment system ORSEE, paid a £3 show-up fee plus earnings from the dictator game task",
  "analysis_plan": "Mann-Whitney tests and OLS regressions testing the effects of treatment, gender, their interactions, and age on the amount allocated to the recipient",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Each session consisted of 70 dictators and 70 recipients with a balanced pool of male and female participants."
}
